classification.difficultyReason: Use cylinder areas to form the cost constraint, follow the supplied volume model, differentiate and interpret the optimum as a base-cost fraction.

content.prompt: An open cylindrical water tank has base radius $x$ metres and height $h$ metres. Each square metre of the base costs $a$ dollars to manufacture and each square metre of the curved surface costs $b$ dollars. The combined cost of the base and curved surface is $c$ dollars.

answer.worked:
The base area is $\pi x^2$ square metres, so its cost is $a\pi x^2$ dollars. The curved surface area is $2\pi xh$ square metres, so its cost is $2\pi bxh$ dollars.
$$c=\pi ax^2+2\pi bxh.$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Show that the volume of the tank is given by $V=\dfrac{x}{2b}(c-\pi ax^2)$.

answer.worked:
$$V=\pi x^2h.$$
From the cost equation,
$$\begin{align*}2\pi bxh&=c-\pi ax^2\\h&=\frac{c-\pi ax^2}{2\pi bx}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore
$$\begin{align*}V&=\pi x^2\times\frac{c-\pi ax^2}{2\pi bx}\\V&=\frac{x}{2b}(c-\pi ax^2).\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: As $x$ varies, prove that $V$ is at its maximum when the cost of the base is $\dfrac{c}{3}$ dollars.

answer.short: The maximum occurs at $x=\sqrt{\dfrac{c}{3\pi a}}$, giving base cost $\pi ax^2=\dfrac{c}{3}$ dollars.
answer.worked:
For a tank with positive dimensions, $a,b,c>0$ and $0<x<\sqrt{\frac{c}{(\pi a)}}$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{dV}{dx}&=\frac{c-3\pi ax^2}{2b}.\end{align*}$$
At a stationary point,
$$\begin{align*}c-3\pi ax^2&=0\\x^2&=\frac{c}{3\pi a}\\x&=\sqrt{\frac{c}{3\pi a}}.\end{align*}$$
This value lies in the domain. Also,
$$\frac{d^2V}{dx^2}=-\frac{3\pi ax}{b}<0$$
throughout the domain, since $a,x,b>0$. Thus the stationary point gives the global maximum volume.
At this radius,
$$\begin{align*}\text{Base cost}&=a\pi x^2\\\text{Base cost}&=a\pi\times\frac{c}{3\pi a}\\\text{Base cost}&=\frac{c}{3}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore the volume is greatest when the base costs $\dfrac{c}{3}$ dollars.
